scope: Actual Linux filesystem helpers in the existing single VM; synthetic temporary files only. This is not product GUI acceptance or evidence of per-Bot parallel desktops.
runtime: /opt/node/bin/node --test; root test process; separate UID/GID 65532 read subprocess

checks.name: Text overwrite and listing compatibility
checks.details: Explicit ordinary-file overwrite, decimal 200000-byte read cap, link name/type listing without traversal.

checks.name: Hard links and symbolic links
checks.details: Read and overwrite reject hard links/final symlinks; workspace-root symlinks rejected including trailing slash. Outside synthetic private content unchanged.

checks.name: Special files
checks.details: FIFO rejected by read/write without blocking; omitted from both listings.

checks.name: Directory replacement race
checks.details: 100 rounds, 600 attempted operations across binary/text reads, both listings, explicit text overwrite and exclusive upload while another thread replaces the parent with an outside symlink. At least 10 actual directory replacements, both successful in-workspace operations and refusals. No outside sentinel content returned/listed; outside read/write canaries and directory entries unchanged.

checks.name: Desktop identity ownership
checks.details: When workspace is UID 65532 and service UID 0, newly created directories/files have UID/GID 65532 via descriptor chown and modes 0700/0600. UID/GID 65532 subprocess actually reads upload bytes. Existing root-owned file owner/mode and ordinary root-owned workspace semantics remain unchanged.

limits: Configured workspace ancestors must remain trusted; workspace root itself is opened without following symlinks.
macOS retains best-effort path validation and is not claimed to provide the Linux descriptor isolation boundary.
Interrupted explicit overwrite may leave a partially modified ordinary workspace file; writes are not rolled back.
